Dylan Larkin’s agent breaks down trade between Canadiens, Red Wings
items.body: The Dylan Larkin saga came to an end after the Detroit Red Wings pulled the trigger on a trade with the Montreal Canadiens Sunday night. The deal was months in the making, but the road to getting the deal done was anything but straightforward, as Larkin's agent, Pat Brisson, detailed on Real Kyper and Bourne Monday afternoon. Brisson said there were many challenges in Detroit but Montreal's emergence as a preferred destination helped pave the way to get a trade completed. He described the final stages as particularly exhausting, revealing that the situation had been building for approximately two months, with the final 10 to 15 days bringing increased activity as the two sides worked toward an agreement. "It was one of those files that you want to hopefully get done the sooner the better, but sometimes it goes longer than expected," Brisson explained. The process officially began in May, when Larkin requested a trade from Detroit. Brisson said the initial hope was to have something completed before the NHL Draft, traditionally a more active period for teams looking to reshape their rosters. However, as Brisson explained, the situation became increasingly complicated when the Red Wings removed Steve Yzerman from the general manager job on July 14. With Detroit lacking permanent leadership in its front office, the trade discussions became more difficult to navigate. Brisson said it was frustrating to watch July and August pass without much traction on a trade as the Red Wings searched for a new head of hockey operations. items.title: Report: Mammoth’s Keller, Guenther to return to lineup vs. Jets
items.summary: Although injuries have riddled the Utah Mammoth over the month of November, they’re poised to regain two of their top forwards.
items.body: Although injuries have riddled the Utah Mammoth over the month of November, they're poised to regain two of their top goal scorers. Mammoth forwards Clayton Keller (illness) and Dylan Guenther (upper body) will return to the lineup on Monday against the Winnipeg Jets, Ken Wiebe of the Winnipeg Free Press reported . Keller's return was expected following a one-game absence while he dealt with an illness, and he'll slot back in alongside Logan Cooley and Vincent Trocheck on Utah's first line. The 11th-year forward has recorded five goals and a team-high 24 assists in 23 games this season, while having missed just the one game. However, the same can't be said for Guenther, who was placed on injured reserve on Nov. 11 and given an initial two-to-four week recovery timeline. While it's unclear how and when he sustained the injury, head coach André Tourigny described the young forward as "pretty banged up" after he missed miss two consecutive practices following the Mammoth's 4-2 loss to the Ottawa Senators on Nov. 7 Fortunately for Utah, he practised in a standard capacity on Friday and is in line to take the ice against Winnipeg for the first time since he faced Ottawa. Through 18 games this season, Guenther has recorded six goals, six assists and a minus-12 rating.

The 3rd overall pick in 2011, who has never played an AHL game, has been working his way back in what has been a tough 2026, to say the least. items.title: Kings’ Erik Gustafsson placed on injured reserve, will miss multiple weeks
items.summary: Although star forward is set to return to the lineup following a four-game absence, the Los Angeles Kings are now set to be without or of their top defencemen for the forseeable future.
items.body: Although a star forward is set to return to the lineup following a four-game absence, the Los Angeles Kings are now set to be without a veteran defenceman for the foreseeable future. The Kings placed defenceman Erik Gustafsson on injured reserve with a non-displaced fracture in his hand and he is expected to miss two to four weeks, the team announced on Tuesday. The move comes as Artemi Panarin returns to the lineup after travelling home to Russia following the death of his grandfather. Although the exact play Gustafsson suffered the injury on remains unknown, he exited following the second period of Saturday's 4-2 loss to the Ottawa Senators and did not return. In his absence, veteran Joel Edmunsson will seemingly slot into the first defensive pairing alongside Brandt Clarke, with Cody Ceci in line to fill the vacant roster spot. Gustafsson, 34, previously missed three games with an undisclosed injury he suffered near the beginning of the month and played in just three upon returning, prior to suffering the fracture. Through 16 games this season, Gustafsson has recorded two goals, seven assists and a zero rating while operating on the Kings' top defensive pairing alongside Clarke.

A 34-year-old left-handed blueliner, Gustafsson joined the Kings this offseason when he signed a one-year, $1 million contract as an unrestricted free agent to provide mobility, puck-moving ability and depth to a Los Angeles defensive unit that needed all of that. Gustafsson has been a bright spot for a Kings team largely lacking them this year. Prior to suffering the injury during Saturday’s 4-2 loss to the Ottawa Senators, the Swede was riding a personal four-game point streak in which he had racked up a goal and four assists. Hage is exactly the type of piece that the Wings were waiting on throughout these negotiation processes. To thin out the forward corps, the Red Wings have placed Sheldon Dries on waivers, per Sportsnet’s Elliotte Friedman . Dries, 32, has already spent more time with Detroit than he expected this year. After spending most of his first two years in the Red Wings organization with the Grand Rapids Griffins in the AHL, Dries inked a two-year, $1.75MM extension with Detroit last February. Primarily an injury replacement, Dries went scoreless in five games for the Red Wings last season. He was exceptional in the AHL, registering 23 goals and 45 points in 57 games with a +20 rating. Unlike last season, Dries has played for the Red Wings more often than not. Since Detroit suspended Larkin without pay, Dries has held down a consistent role in the Red Wings’ lineup. Still, he hasn’t been that productive, registering only one assist in 16 games while averaging 10:06 of ice time per game. In his brief time with the Griffins this season, Dries has scored five goals and eight points in games with a +4 rating. Still, although he hasn’t been as offensively fruitful as he has been in the AHL, Dries has found other ways to contribute. Before being placed on waivers, Dries was fifth on the team in hits (34), and he has held his own defensively, maintaining a 90.7% on-ice SV%, good for 11th on the team.

items.body: Defenseman will miss second straight game against Sharks on Monday VANCOUVER -- Quinn Hughes was placed on injured reserve with an undisclosed injury and will miss the conclusion of the Minnesota Wild's three-game road trip at the San Jose Sharks on Monday (10 p.m. ET; Wild+, MINNHL, NBCSCA, SN360, SN). The defenseman was being further evaluated after he left a 4-1 win at the Calgary Flames on Thursday following a hit from Flames forward Adam Klapka at 9:57 of the third period. Wild coach John Hynes did not have an update after the game and declined to specify the nature of the injury prior to a 4-3 shootout loss at the Vancouver Canucks on Saturday, but a concussion has been ruled out. “He's not going to play on the trip, so he's going to go back to Minny and get reevaluated now and we’ll have some more info,” Hynes said before the game. Hughes has 21 points (six goals, 15 assists) during a NHL career high 13 -game point streak (including a goal and an assist Thursday) that set a Wild record for defensemen. Hughes ranks second among NHL defensemen with 34 points (eight goals, 26 assists) in 24 games. He leads all skaters in time on ice per game (27:49) and is plus-15. “There's not a lot of people that can replace what he does on a nightly basis, offensively, defensively, the way he controls the game, so you'll miss that,” Wild forward Nick Foligno said of Hughes. “But we’ve got so much confidence in the guys in this room that will make up for it and pick up the slack like he does when other guys are out.” Saturday would have been Hughes’ second trip back to Vancouver since he was traded to Minnesota on Dec. 12, 2025. items.body: Add to Preferred Sources The leadership group in one of the Professional Women’s Hockey League’s newest teams has been revealed. All three players were foundational signings for the new organization in Southern Ontario, signed by the Havoc during Phase 2 of the PWHL Expansion Player Distribution Process. Having grown up in nearby Oakville, I understand what hockey means to this community and the passion that exists throughout the region. We have a wonderful opportunity ahead of us in a great hockey city, and I’m excited to help build something new and meaningful for the community. I’m proud to be a part of it and look forward to what we can accomplish together.” Jenner is one of the most decorated players of her generation. Having been a member of the Canadian National Team since the 2012 IIHF Women’s World Championship, the Oakville, Ont. native has won gold at the Women’s Worlds four times, with two gold medals at the Winter Olympics. He will provide extra depth after Martin Pospisil was injured in Saturday’s loss to the Chicago Blackhawks. Calgary seemed prepared for Morton’s recall, with the centerman being held out of the Wranglers’ Sunday matchup. Morton will now receive his first call-up of the season, and his first since signing a one-year extension with Calgary over the summer. The 27 year old has scored six points, eight penalty minutes, and a minus-three in 20 games with the Wranglers this season. He has been a go-to depth forward through the last two seasons – though that role has only resulted in Morton making four NHL appearances. He’s marked those games with one goal and 10 penalty minutes. Morton has otherwise been productive in the minor-league. He reached a career-high 45 points in 70 games of the 2024-25 season, good for the fifth-most points on the Wranglers that season. He repeated that standing last season, notching 38 points in 68 games to rank fifth again. The Flames will have Morton as an option for Monday’s matchup against the Ottawa Senators. They will decide between Morton and Brennan Othmann to fill the hole left open by Pospisil. Othmann has yet to score through seven games this season. He notched two points in as many games with Calgary last season, after joining the team via trade ahead of the 2026 Trade Deadline. Monday’s matchup could represent another chance to help Othmann find his groove. If not, Calgary will have the gritty Morton to help replace Pospisil’s physical presence.

items.title: Dylan Larkin to make Canadiens debut against Kings
items.body: One day after acquiring him, the Montreal Canadiens will have new centre Dylan Larkin in the lineup. Larkin will suit up for a team other than the Detroit Red Wings for the first time in his NHL career Monday night as he makes his Canadiens debut against the Los Angeles Kings (Sportsnet+, 7 p.m. ET / 5 p.m. PCT), the team announced . After 11-plus seasons in Detroit, Larkin was traded to Montreal for a package that included forward Kirby Dach, goalie Sam Montembeault and top prospect Michael Hage and plenty of draft capital on Sunday. Larkin was drafted by Detroit in 2014 with the 15th-overall pick. He requested a trade in the off-season and was finally granted his wish on Sunday, ending a months-long saga. In 10 games played with the Red Wings this season, the 30 year-old has two goals and six points.

Initially, Detroit was steadfast in its belief that any Larkin swap must return a similar player who could step right into the lineup. General manager Meghan Duggan has signed some of the best available players through expansion and recruited a top-level coach in Kris Sparre . Canada’s newest expansion franchise looks to provide southern Ontario with a winning team that it desperately wants. The Havoc will play their first-ever regular-season game on the road against the Montreal Victoire on Dec. 5. One week later, their home opener is against the Ottawa Charge. Unlike the PWHL’s two expansion teams from last season, the Havoc have a chance to generate plenty of offense in 2026-27. They signed one of the biggest free agents this summer in Brianne Jenner , who set new career highs last season with 12 goals and 26 points. She will be joined by her former Charge teammate Emily Clark , who after an impressive 2024-25 campaign signed a record-breaking, six-figure contract but struggled mightily in 2025-26. Another key forward signed by Duggan was Alina Muller, whose 21 points helped her finish third in team scoring with the Boston Fleet last season. She will be expected to continue providing depth scoring for the Havoc. One skater who could provide an offensive boost is Nicole Gosling. The former Victoire defender had a dominant rookie season, as she finished with three goals and 19 points and led the team with 21:17 of average ice time. Gosling was also a major factor in Montreal’s Walter Cup championship and is expected to bring that championship pedigree to Hamilton. items.title: Grading the Dylan Larkin trade: Canadiens, Red Wings complete Atlantic Division blockbuster
items.summary: As Montreal gets its 2C, Detroit gears up for a fresh start.
items.body: Add to Preferred Sources Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect We can’t say we weren’t expecting big news out of Detroit, but the Red Wings and Montreal Canadiens managed to surprise us nonetheless with a true in-division blockbuster that could change the landscape of the Eastern Conference. The Habs ended a years-long search for a second high-end center, Dylan Larkin, to pair with captain Nick Suzuki. The Red Wings, meanwhile, shipped out the signature player of their long, frustrating wilderness years in exchange for a package that could kickstart a new era of success. Larkin asked out of Detroit in June, shortly after the end of the Wings’ 10th consecutive season without playoff hockey. The American centerman’s full trade protection and the Red Wings’ bizarre willingness to go without a GM for most of the offseason made a clean break unlikely. Still, when Larkin left the team after 10 awkward games with the captain’s ‘C’ stripped from his jersey, his eventual departure became a formality. The question was how Horcoff could get fair value for a very good player and his very reasonable contract; reports suggested Larkin would only waive his veto power to go to a contending team in America. Turns out, at least one team could lure him north of the border. Larkin is off to aid Les Habitants in their quest for Stanley Cup No. 25, as Kirby Dach, Sam Montembeault, the rights to top prospect Michael Hage, and a pile of draft picks go the other direction in Horcoff’s first major trade at the helm of an embattled Detroit club. Did Horcoff get enough to justify trading a top player to a division rival? And is Larkin good enough to elevate the young, hungry Habs from a playoff team to a Stanley Cup favorite? items.title: Engels: Larkin worth the hefty price Canadiens paid Red Wings
items.summary: The Canadiens and GM Kent Hughes pulled off the practically impossible, acquiring Dylan Larkin to fill a burning hole on their roster. Eric Engels explains why Montreal was right to pay the price in Sunday’s trade with the Red Wings.
items.body: Let that sink in for a second before we get into what general manager Kent Hughes gave up to make it happen. Because getting a second-line centre is an extremely difficult endeavour in this league, but getting one who’s been a first-line centre for the last 11 seasons is practically impossible and Hughes has officially pulled it off here. It took Larkin asking out of Detroit and putting Montreal on the list of cities he was willing to accept a trade to for the opportunity to arise, and it took major negotiating from Hughes with Red Wings interim GM Shawn Horcoff to get the price down from “prohibitive,” as league sources labelled it weeks ago , to acceptable. One Western Conference executive we touched base with right after the trade was consummated late Sunday night praised Montreal's GM, saying, “You only get a couple of cracks at this.” The Canadiens bought themselves at least four cracks at it—and probably five—by shipping out A-level prospect Michael Hage as the headliner on their side of the deal to acquire Larkin, who’s signed through the end of the 2030-31 season for just $8.7 million per year. It could be at least five if/when Canadiens first-line centre Nick Suzuki extends beyond 2030, when his current $7.875-million cap hit is set to expire. But for now, with both Suzuki and Larkin making under $9 million per season, and with the rest of the Canadiens core locked in under $9.5 million per through 2031, a very hard decision became easier to make for Hughes. He came in at the onset of a rebuild in 2022 with hopes of quickly turning the Canadiens into perennial Stanley Cup contenders, and after four years of methodically getting them to the precipice, he had a chance to push them over the edge with one swift move and took it. items.summary: The surging St. Louis Blues overcame a three-goal deficit in the final 10 minutes of regulation for the first time in franchise history and then beat the Edmonton Oilers in a shootout for a dramatic 5-4 victory on Sunday night for their fourth straight win.
items.body: ST. LOUIS — The surging St. Louis Blues overcame a three-goal deficit in the final 10 minutes of regulation for the first time in franchise history and then beat the Edmonton Oilers in a shootout for a dramatic 5-4 victory on Sunday night for their fourth straight win. Dalibor Dvorsky, Philip Broberg, Pavel Buchnevich and Jimmy Snuggerud each scored for the Blues (13-9-2), who have netted 26 goals during their current four-game win streak. St. Louis, which beat New Jersey 9-6 at home on Saturday, is 8-3-1 at the Enterprise Center this season. Broberg, Buchnevich and Snuggerud all scored within a stretch of 5:11 in the third period. Snuggerud’s team-leading 14th goal of the season tied the score at 4-4 with 4:42 remaining in regulation. Jake Neighbors and Mason McTavish scored shootout goals for the Blues. Goalie Joel Hofer allowed a goal by Connor McDavid but then stopped shots from Leon Draisaitl and Owen Michaels on the Oilers’ final two attempts. Draisaitl scored a second-period goal and became the ninth player in franchise history (72nd the in NHL) to reach 1,100 career points. The 31-year-old has 457 goals and 643 assists in 881 career games. Kasperi Kapanen had a goal and an assist for the Oilers against his former team, and Filip Hallander and Colton Dach added goals. McDavid, Evan Bouchard, Connor Murphy, Mathieu Joseph, Vasily Podkolzin and Jason Dickinson each had an assist. The Pacific Division-leading Oilers (17-5-4) have lost three straight overall and fell to 10-2-2 on the road this season.

However, things simply haven’t gone right this year for him. As a result, TSN’s Darren Dreger reported in a recent Insider Trading segment that GM Kevin Cheveldayoff is trying to drum up interest in the veteran. The 34-year-old was a consistent 30-plus-point scorer up until the 2024-25 season. He had 18 goals in his first season with Winnipeg, helping to earn him a three-year, $12MM deal along the way. Niederreiter is now in the final season of that agreement, a backloaded one that carries a $3.5MM salary this year. But after a 17-goal effort in the first year of the contract, things have gone in the wrong direction. Niederreiter’s production dipped to eight goals and 11 assists in 61 games last season while his ice time dipped to under 14 minutes per night. This season, things have been even worse. Niederreiter has been held off the scoresheet in 11 games where he’s logging a career-low 11:07 per night. He has also been scratched for 12 contests. items.body: The long-time Detroit Red Wings forward has been traded to the Montreal Canadiens in a deal announced on Sunday. Montreal acquired Larkin, along with a 2028 second-round pick and 2027 third-round pick, in exchange for forward Kirby Dach, goaltender Samuel Montembeault, the rights to forward Michael Hage, a first-round pick in 2027, a second-round pick in 2027, a fourth-round pick in 2028 and a first-round pick in 2029. Larkin initially requested a trade in April after the Red Wings missed the playoffs for a 10th straight year, but due to leadership changes in the front office, talks stalled throughout the off-season. The 30-year-old was then stripped of his captaincy that he had held for his hometown team since 2021, but still reported to Detroit and played 10 games before stepping away from the team in October — leading to a suspension without pay and forfeiting over $1 million in salary — until a resolution materialized. items.title: Montreal Canadiens Acquire Dylan Larkin In Massive Package Deal With Detroit Red Wings
items.summary: The Montreal Canadiens and Detroit Red Wings agree to a massive package deal that includes Dylan Larkin.
items.body: David Kirouac-Imagn Images David Kirouac-Imagn Images Montreal Canadiens Acquire Dylan Larkin In Massive Package Deal With Detroit Red Wings Andre Leal Partner Nov 23, 2026 1:52 AM Published Nov 23, 2026 1:52 AM Updated Nov 23, 2026 2:20 AM The Montreal Canadiens and Detroit Red Wings agree to a massive package deal that includes Dylan Larkin. The Dylan Larkin saga is officially over as the Detroit Red Wings and Montreal Canadiens agreed on a package trade to send the former captain north of the border . Along with Larkin, the Canadiens received a 2028 second-round pick and a 2027 third-round pick. The Red Wings received seven assets in this trade. items.title: Tage Thompson scores twice as Sabres top Lightning
items.body: TAMPA, Fla. — Tage Thompson scored twice, Zach Benson had a goal and two assists and Ukko-Pekka Luukkonen finished with 29 saves and the Buffalo Sabres beat the Tampa Bay Lightning 6-2 on Sunday. Noah Ostlund had a goal and two points. Jack Quinn and Jiri Kulich also scored for Buffalo. Nikita Kucherov and Gage Goncalves scored for Tampa Bay, which suffered only its second loss on home ice this season in 12 games (10-2-0). Dennis Hildeby finished with 22 saves to suffer his first regulation loss this season in his sixth start. Thompson has goals in four consecutive games and 12 goals in his past 12 games. His 33rd career multi-goal game ties Pat LaFontaine for 10th most in franchise history. Thompson's two goals 5:12 apart in the second period broke open the game for Buffalo. He scored on a one-timer from the left circle for a 5-on-3 power play goal for a 3-1 lead then danced around Pontus Holmberg, who lost his stick, to get to the middle slot for a wrist shot at 16:17. It was the 18th multi-goal period for Thompson, tying Dave Andreychuk for fifth most in franchise history. Quinn increased his goal-scoring streak to three games, converting a 2-on-1 chance 1:22 into the second period to break a 1-1 tie. Goncalves notched his first of the season to bring the Lightning to within 4-2 at 5:50 of the third period, but Ostlund put Buffalo back ahead by three goals a minute later. items.body: Register Login Wyatt Kaiser Receives Three-Game Suspension By Brian La Rose | at November 22, 2026 6:32 pm Speaking to reporters including Mark Lazerus of The Athletic after yesterday’s game against Calgary, Blackhawks defenseman Wyatt Kaiser didn’t seem too concerned about the prospect of potential supplemental discipline for his hit on Flames forward Martin Pospisil : “Not really, to be honest . Because at the end of the day, if they really look at it and say, hey, that’s really dangerous, (then) you’re suspended for a game or two, take a fine, and then you’re back. … We’ll see what they say.” It turned out that the league did indeed feel the hit was really dangerous. The Department of Player Safety went a little longer than Kaiser’s suggestion as well, announcing that the blueliner has received a three-game ban for the hit. The video breakdown of the suspension from the league can be viewed here . The incident occurred late in the second period of Saturday’s contest. Pospisil left the game with an upper-body injury and did not return while Kaiser received a match penalty on the play, which carried an automatic league review. This is the first suspension of Kaiser’s career and the first to be handed out to a Blackhawk since Brett Connolly received a four-game ban for interference back in 2021. items.body: Register Login Blue Jackets Reassign Steven Lorentz By Brennan McClain | at November 22, 2026 5:31 pm According to a team announcement , the Columbus Blue Jackets have assigned forward Steven Lorentz to the Cleveland Monsters in the AHL. The move allows the Blue Jackets to activate injured winger Conor Garland whenever he recovers from his upper-body injury. Although he wasn’t supposed to be, Lorentz was included in the return package to the Blue Jackets in the Kirill Marchenko trade. Because the Toronto Maple Leafs signed Marchenko to an extension as part of the trade, they had to square that with the 2027-28 salary cap. Since Lorentz is on a $1.35MM salary through the 2027-28 campaign, Columbus accepted him back to facilitate the deal. It was clear relatively early that Columbus didn’t plan to have Lorentz on the roster. After clearing waivers a few days before the trade, the Blue Jackets cut Lorentz from their opening-night roster, and he began the season in Cleveland. Lorentz played really well with the Monsters. Through the first month of the regular season, Lorentz scored seven goals and nine points in nine games with a +2 rating, until the Blue Jackets recalled him on November 5th. Since his call-up, the 30-year-old forward has gone scoreless in seven games while averaging 8:04 of ice time per game. Even if Garland isn’t ready to go quite yet, the clock was ticking on Lorentz’s waiver eligibility. If he had played three more games, or spent 13 more days on Columbus’ active roster, Lorentz would have required waivers again for another demotion. Because they reassigned him today, the Blue Jackets will pause that clock for now.

items.body: NEW YORK — Jackson Blake put Carolina ahead to stay midway through the second period and Brandon Bussi made 25 saves and the Carolina Hurricanes defeated the New York Rangers 5-2 on Sunday. Blake snapped a 1-1 tie on the backhand at 13:13, followed in quick succession by goals from defencemen Alexander Nikishin and Sean Walker as the first-place Hurricanes won for the sixth time in seven games. Mika Zibanejad and J. T. Miller scored for the Rangers, who had their three-game winning streak snapped. Eric Robinson also scored for the defending champion Hurricanes, who are an Eastern Conference-best 18-3-3. Robinson opened the scoring with a short-handed goal at the 13-minute mark of the first, beating Rangers netminder Dylan Garand for his third goal. Zibanejad tied it on the power play at 14:12 of the opening period with his sixth goal. The 33-year-old Zibanejad is sixth in Rangers history with 687 points, four points behind Mark Messier for fifth place. Blake put the visitors ahead finishing off a passing play with linemates Taylor Hall and Logan Stankoven for his seventh goal. Nikishin made it 3-1 at 17:46. Walker, playing his 500th game, extended the lead to 4-1 at 18:27. Miller made it 4-2 on the power play at 15:13 of the third before Jordan Martinook scored into an empty net. The Rangers hadn’t played since Monday’s 3-1 home win over Montreal. New York lost for only the third time in 12 games at Madison Square Garden. Bussi, who won 31 games last season and three in the Cup Final after he was claimed off waivers, improved to 5-2-2. Rangers newcomer Max Sasson — acquired Friday from Vancouver — skated on a line with Glenn Gawdin and Matt Rempe. Rangers forward Pavel Dorofeyev missed his second straight game with a lower-body injury.

items.body: Add to Preferred Sources Credit: David Banks-Imagn Images The NHL Department of Player Safety (DoPS) wasted little time deciding on a punishment for Chicago Blackhawks defenseman Wyatt Kaiser. The NHL DoPS announced on Sunday that Kaiser has been suspended three games for his illegal hit on Calgary Flames forward Martin Pospisil during Chicago’s 4-3 overtime win on Saturday. The hit occured late in the second period when Pospisil was attempting to skate the puck out of his own zone, and Kaiser came across to deliver a direct blow to Pospisil’s head with his shoulder near Calgary’s blueline. Kaiser was assessed a five-minute major and game misconduct for the hit. In a video released by the NHL DPos, it was explained that Kaiser’s hit satisfies both element of the Illegal Check to the Head rule. “First, the head is the main point of contact,” the video states. “Kaiser takes a poor angle of approach and cuts across the front of Pospisil’s body, missing his core and making direct contact with his head. And, it is Pospisil’s head that absorbs the vast majority of the force. While Pospisil is stickhandling and does pull the puck towards his body prior to the check, his head stays level and moves predictably. He does not change the position of his head or body just prior to or simultaneously with contact in a way that significantly contributes to the head being the main point of contact.” Pospisil’s status remains unclear, but he left Saturday’s game and did not return. Kaiser, 24, had not been levied any discipline from the league prior to this suspension. items.title: Canadiens loan Brett Berard, David Reinbacher to AHL
items.summary: Forward Brett Berard and defenceman David Reinbacher have been loaned to the American Hockey League’s Laval Rocket, the team announced Sunday.
items.body: The Montreal Canadiens are juggling their roster after a last-minute loss to the Philadelphia Flyers on Saturday night. Forward Brett Berard and defenceman David Reinbacher have been loaned to the American Hockey League's Laval Rocket, the team announced Sunday. Both players were recent call-ups and suited up in Montreal's 4-3 loss to the Flyers. Berard played 7:10 in the defeat but notched his first assist at the NHL level since the 2024-25 season. The 24-year-old has played three games this year since being called up to the Canadiens on Wednesday. Since making his NHL debut in the 2024-25 season, the Providence, R.I., native has six goals and five assists in 51 games. Reinbacher, meanwhile, was playing in only his second game of the year against Philadelphia. Though he finished without a point — and has yet to record one this season — he had 10 minutes of ice time with three shots on goal. The fifth-overall pick has only made four appearances with one point at the NHL level since being drafted in 2023. The Canadiens (14-6-4) get back to action on Monday as they play host to the Los Angeles Kings.

items.summary: The last time three teammates finished 1-2-3 atop league scoring was 1940. But with the Oilers off to a hot start, Michael Amato explores whether Connor McDavid, Leon Draisaitl and Evan Bouchard could pull it off in his Sunday Overreactions.
items.body: Even for the most optimistic Edmonton Oilers fan, it would’ve been hard to envision a better start to the season. The Oilers are getting saves, playing better defensively and are being powered by three elite offensive talents — so much so that Connor McDavid , Leon Draisaitl and Evan Bouchard are all sitting in the top five in league scoring after 25 games and appear to be showing no signs of slowing down. You’d have to go all the way back to 1940 to find a season where the top three scorers in the NHL at the end of the campaign were all on the same team. It's a seemingly impossible feat in what is now an 84-game season and considering Bouchard plays defence, but if anyone can get it done, it may be this Oilers trio. McDavid, Draisaitl and Bouchard will finish as the top three scorers this season As it stands, McDavid is first, Draisaitl second and Bouchard is fourth, a handful of points back of Kirill Kaprizov for third spot. There are a few things that could be working in their favour, too. Nikita Kucherov is still having a great year, but he’s scoring at a lower point pace than he has in the past four seasons. We also just learned that Nathan MacKinnon is set to miss the next 12 weeks with an injury, so he won’t be a factor when it comes to the league leaders. Quinn Hughes, who is just behind Bouchard in the scoring race, is also now sidelined with an ailment. items.title: 2026-27 PWHL team preview: Detroit Clutch
items.summary: One of the league’s newest franchises has the tools to make an immediate impact in their first season.
items.body: Add to Preferred Sources Credit: PWHL After numerous successful Takeover Tour games, it was only a matter of time before Hockeytown got its own Professional Women’s Hockey League team. After being passed over in the first wave of expansion in 2025, the Motor City finally has its chance to shine in the women’s hockey world. The team, appropriately named the Detroit Clutch , isn’t just expected to draw the attention of a hockey-mad region, but it’s expected to do well in its first season. With a roster orchestrated by the legend Manon Rheaume , the Charge are looking like a true Walter Cup Playoff contender heading into their inaugural campaign. Sure, there has already been some controversy with the franchise, with the Hilary Knight sign-and-trade gaining plenty of criticism across the game. Yet, that doesn’t deter the notion that the Clutch have a talented roster that can hang with the original six franchises, giving hockey fans in Detroit something to cheer about for the first time in a decade. Former Wild player Marco Rossi , part of the four-for-one blockbuster trade 11 months ago that sent Canucks captain Quinn Hughes to Minnesota, scored his second goal of the game with 1:23 left in regulation time and Vancouver skating with an extra attacker. One of the Canucks’ overtime shifts featured Rossi, Buium and former Wild player Liam Ohgren together, and Buium came close to winning the game when he dashed in from left wing and forced a strong save from Jesper Wallstedt. Canuck goalie Leevi Merilainen made 22 saves, including a breakaway stop on Joel Eriksson Ek in overtime, plus two more in the shootout before Kirill Kaprisov’s final attempt clanged off the post to leave Vancouver with its first home-ice victory since Oct. 3. “Seeing Marco score those two felt really good,” Buium said. “And I thought Ohgie played amazing as well. items.body: Explanation: The play on the ice was challenged under Rule 38 – Coach’s Challenge. Rule 38.1 states, “In all Coach’s Challenge situations, the original call on the ice will be overturned if, and only if, a conclusive and irrefutable determination can be made on the basis of video evidence that the original call on the ice was clearly not correct. If a review is not conclusive and/or there is any doubt whatsoever as to whether the call on the ice was correct, the original call on the ice will be confirmed.” After a thorough examination of all available replays, video review determined that Jacob Trouba ’s shot from the defending zone subsequently deflected off Bobby McMann ’s stick before going out of play . The decision was made in accordance with Rule 38.2 (d) which states, in part, that a team may request a Coach’s Challenge “When a minor penalty for delaying the game has been assessed under Rule 63.2 (iii) for shooting or batting the puck out of play from the defending zone. This will only apply to delay of game penalties when the shot/batted puck is determined to have subsequently deflected off a player, stick, glass or boards, etc., and not a judgment call.” Therefore, the delay of game penalty assessed to Jacob Trouba was rescinded.

items.body: TORONTO — Of all the Toronto Maple Leafs ’ nine consecutive losses, of all eight straight on home ice, and of all 11 they’ve swallowed in their past 12 attempts, this was the ugliest. items.title: Fowler shows he’s human as Canadiens fall to Flyers in final minute
items.summary: Jacob Fowler has already proven he can handle just about anything this league can shoot at him. But on Saturday, the young netminder allowed a late goal that sank the Canadiens against the Flyers.
items.body: MONTREAL — Disappointment burned from Jacob Fowler ’s eyes as he stood in his crease, shaking his head, trying to shake off the goal he’d just surrendered with 31 seconds left in what turned out to be a 4-3 loss for his Montreal Canadiens to the Philadelphia Flyers. It was something we haven’t seen from the young goaltender since he debuted last season, which says everything about who Fowler has been in the NHL. “He’s been our best player,” said Noah Dobson, who was far from being one of Montreal’s better ones in this loss to Philadelphia. Still, the Canadiens were good enough to at least earn a point. They came out of a dominant first tied 1-1, despite Fowler having surrendered one of two shots he faced. They gave up several odd-man rushes in the second and Fowler was beat on more than the one that put the Flyers up 2-1, with shots ringing off the bars behind him before Rasmus Ristolainen made it 3-1 from 60 feet out. And after they played their best hockey of the night in the third, with goals from Zachary Bolduc and Owen Beck coming 74 seconds apart to tie the game, Fowler did something else he never does. He had squared up to Matvei Michkov’s 49-foot, harmless shot, waved his glove at it and, instead of closing it on the puck, deflected it right to Sean Couturier, who scooped up the puck and fed Noah Cates the easiest goal he’ll probably get this season. All Fowler could do after that was watch helplessly as the Canadiens scrambled to tie the game with too little time left on the clock. “He’s human, he’s going to make mistakes,” said Beck, offering up a truth no one should ignore. Least of all Fowler, who’d have probably said he hated that last goal he gave up as much as the first one—even if it was a perfect tip of a wide shot that was virtually impossible to stop.

items.body: Register Login Ducks’ Leo Carlsson Exits With Upper-Body Injury By Gabriel Foley | at November 21, 2026 10:06 pm The Anaheim Ducks lost top center Leo Carlsson to an apparent upper-body injury during Saturday’s matchup with the Utah Mammoth. Carlsson sustained the injury on a hit that sandwiched him between Utah defenseman Mikhail Sergachev and a referee. He was helped off the ice by a trainer. Anaheim announced before the third period that Carlsson would not return. Carlsson became the highest-paid player in the NHL thanks to an offer sheet from the Philadelphia Flyers over the summer. He has followed Anaheim’s historic match with a career-best start to the season. Carlsson has 22 assists and 29 points in 24 games this season, including Saturday night. He has been the setup man to Cutter Gauthier who leads the team with 21 goals and 30 points. In their time together, at all strengths, Carlsson and Gauthier have outscored opponents 32-to-12. They even came together for Anaheim’s opening tally on Saturday, with Gauthier recording the only assist on Carlsson’s seventh goal of the season. The Ducks bumped Mikael Granlund up the lineup in Carlsson’s absence. Granlund could be the ideal playmaker to keep Gauthier’s hot scoring rolling without the Ducks’ star. Named Anaheim’s captain over the summer, Granlund is off to a red-hot start of his own with 26 points in 22 games. He could reach the first 70-point season of his career this year, after passing 60 points five times through 15 seasons in the NHL. Granlund’s lead over the Ducks’ lineup will become even more important as Anaheim moves forward without their $18MM centerman.
